words.meaning: The rational principle that governs and develops the universe.
words.sentence1: Ancient Greek philosophers sought to understand the underlying logos of the cosmos. (Ancient Greek philosophers sought to understand the underlying logos of the cosmos.)
words.sentence2: In rhetoric, logos appeals to reason and logical arguments. (In rhetoric, logos appeals to reason and logical arguments.)

words.meaning: The ability to judge well or perceive clearly.
words.sentence1: Se necesita gran discernimiento para navegar por los dilemas morales de la vida. (Great discernment is needed to navigate life's moral dilemmas.)
words.sentence2: Su discernimiento le permitió ver la verdad más allá de las apariencias. (Her discernment allowed her to see the truth beyond appearances.)

words.meaning: Clarity of expression, thought, or perception; mental sharpness.
words.sentence1: Il a analysé la situation avec une grande lucidité philosophique. (He analyzed the situation with great philosophical lucidity.)
words.sentence2: La lucidité est essentielle pour affronter les complexités de l'existence. (Clarity of mind is essential for facing the complexities of existence.)

words.meaning: A particular philosophy or view of life; the worldview of an individual or group.
words.sentence1: Seine philosophische Weltanschauung wurde stark von Immanuel Kant geprägt. (His philosophical worldview was strongly shaped by Immanuel Kant.)
words.sentence2: Jede Epoche hat ihre eigene kulturelle Weltanschauung. (Every epoch has its own cultural worldview.)

words.meaning: A Japanese Buddhist term for awakening, comprehension, or understanding.
words.sentence1: Zazen no jissen wa satori e no michi to shite shirareru. (The practice of seated meditation is known as the path to satori.)
words.sentence2: Kare wa tennen no utsukushisa no naka de fukai satori o eta. (He attained a deep awakening amidst the beauty of nature.)

words.meaning: The action of looking thoughtfully at something for a long time; deep reflective thought.
words.sentence1: La contemplazione della natura porta spesso a una profonda pace interiore. (The contemplation of nature often leads to deep inner peace.)
words.sentence2: I filosofi antichi dedicavano molte ore alla contemplazione dell'universo. (Ancient philosophers dedicated many hours to the contemplation of the universe.)

words.meaning: Ultimate purpose, tenet, or guiding principle in philosophy and life.
words.sentence1: Zhè ge zhéxué liúbái de zōngzhǐ shì zhuiqiu nèixīn de píngjìng. (The guiding principle of this philosophical school is the pursuit of inner peace.)
words.sentence2: Wǒmen de rensheng zōngzhǐ yinggai shi chuandao shanliang. (Our purpose in life should be to spread kindness.)

words.meaning: Reflective thinking, deep contemplation, or meditation.
words.sentence1: In-ganui bonseong-e daehan sangsak-eun oelaen cheolhakja-ui simjang-eul chaewossda. (Deep contemplation on human nature filled the ancient philosopher's heart.)
words.sentence2: Jeon-yeog no-eul-eul bomyeo geuneun gipeun sangsak-e jamgessda. (Watching the evening sunset, he fell into deep reflection.)

words.meaning: Peace, tranquility, and harmony in philosophy and society.
words.sentence1: Prachya samai boran chob kar saom ounchea pi santiphap knong chet. (Ancient philosophy favored cultivating peace within the heart.)
words.sentence2: Santiphap pka lout trauv kar kar sâsân pi mnusset lke. (Inner peace blossoms through the wisdom of humankind.)

words.meaning: A concept, idea, or mental image born from philosophical reflection.
words.sentence1: Hierdie diep denkbeeld vorm die kern van moderne etiek. (This deep concept forms the core of modern ethics.)
words.sentence2: Elke filosoof probeer om sy eie unieke denkbeeld te verduidelik. (Every philosopher tries to explain their own unique mental concept.)
